mathgap.title: Directed More-Than Interpretation
mathgap.principle: Translate comparative statements of the form "A has N more (or fewer) items than B" into the equation A = B + N (or A = B - N), preserving the direction of the comparison.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a sentence uses "has N more (or fewer) ... than" to compare two people's counts.
mathgap.example: Interpreting "A has 5 more items than B" as |A - B| = 5 or as A = B - 5, which loses the direction.

mathgap.title: Immediate Direct Assignment Update
mathgap.principle: A direct count statement (e.g., "A has N items") sets the current value of A to N at that point in the sequence, overriding any previous value for A.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When encountering a sentence that directly states a person's count.
mathgap.example: Treating "A has 7 items" as a permanent constraint that cannot be changed by later transfers.

mathgap.title: Temporal Consistency of Transfers and Relational Statements
mathgap.principle: Process statements in the given order; apply each transfer, split, or redistribution immediately before interpreting later statements that refer to the updated counts.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a transfer or redistribution statement appears, update the involved counts before processing subsequent statements.
mathgap.example: Delaying a "A gives 3 items to B" until after all other statements, causing later references to use outdated counts.

mathgap.title: Full Difference Equality Interpretation
mathgap.principle: Translate sentences equating two differences into the signed form (A - B) = (C - D), preserving the order of names on each side, and allowing either side to be negative.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement says "the number of X has more than Y is equal to the difference between the number of A and B".
mathgap.example: Interpreting such a sentence as |X - Y| = |A - B|, which loses sign information.

mathgap.title: Quantity Modification (Multiplication and Subtraction) – Correct Interpretation
mathgap.principle: When a statement modifies a count by multiplication (e.g., "X increases by N times"), treat it as multiplying the current value by (1 + N) for an increase, or by (1 - N) for a decrease, handling fractional N appropriately.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement uses phrasing like "increases by N times" or "decreases by N times".
mathgap.example: Interpreting "X increases by 2 times" as X = X + 2 instead of X = X * 2.

mathgap.title: Redistribute Equally Among Group
mathgap.principle: If a group of people redistributes their items so that each ends up with an equal amount, compute the total items among the group and divide by the number of people to find each final count.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement says that a set of people share or redistribute items equally.
mathgap.example: Assuming each person keeps their original amount after an "equal redistribution" statement, rather than setting all to the average.

mathgap.title: Comprehensive Constraint Extraction
mathgap.principle: Gather every constraint implied by each statement, even those that do not directly involve the queried person, to build a complete system of equations before solving.
mathgap.when_to_apply: For any problem, extract all relationships, direct counts, transfers, and difference equalities before attempting to compute the answer.
mathgap.example: Ignoring a relational statement that does not mention the target person, missing a necessary equation that determines the target's count.

mathgap.title: Signed Difference Interpretation
mathgap.principle: Treat both "the number of X has more than Y" and "the difference between the number of X and Y" as signed subtraction (X - Y), not as absolute value.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a statement refers to a difference or "more than" relationship.
mathgap.example: Interpreting "X has more than Y" as |X - Y| = N, losing the sign and potentially swapping the direction.

mathgap.title: Difference Equality Numeric Evaluation
mathgap.principle: When a difference equality (A - B = C - D) involves variables whose values are already known, compute the numeric result and use it to solve for the remaining unknowns.
mathgap.when_to_apply: After enough variables have been assigned, evaluate any remaining difference equalities numerically.
mathgap.example: Leaving (A - B) = 5 unevaluated when A and B are already known, missing the chance to solve for another variable.

mathgap.title: Fractional Increase Interpretation
mathgap.principle: Interpret statements of the form "the number of X increases by N/D times" as multiplying the current count by (1 + N/D), not by N/D alone.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement uses a fractional multiplier to describe an increase.
mathgap.example: Interpreting "X increases by 1/2 times" as X = X * 1/2 instead of X = X * (1 + 1/2).

mathgap.description: Treating ‘difference between the number of X and Y’ as absolute value instead of signed subtraction.
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model assumes "difference" means magnitude, ignoring the order of the names.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Always interpret "difference between X and Y" as the signed subtraction X - Y, preserving the order given.

mathgap.description: Delaying the effect of transfer statements until after all other statements.
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model treats transfers as global constraints rather than sequential events.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Apply each transfer immediately when it appears, updating the donor's and recipient's counts before processing later statements.

mathgap.description: Considering a direct count as a fixed initial value that cannot be changed by later transfers.
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model assumes direct counts are immutable initial conditions.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Recognize that a direct assignment sets the current value at that point, but later transfers can modify it.

mathgap.description: Misinterpreting a difference equality as a direct assignment to a single variable, ignoring the second term (including assuming positivity).
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model simplifies the equation incorrectly, dropping the subtraction and treating it as a magnitude equality.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Preserve the full signed form (A - B = C - D) and solve using both sides, keeping sign information.

mathgap.description: Misinterpreting 'increases by N times' (including fractional N) as addition, division, or incorrect multiplication factor (e.g., using N/D instead of 1+N/D).
mathgap.why_it_happens: Confusion between "increase to N times" and "increase by N times", and mishandling of fractional multipliers.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Apply the correct factor: multiply by (1 + N) for whole-number increases, or (1 + N/D) for fractional increases.
